questions.question: A company introduces a new CRM system but only installs the software and migrates the customer database. Using Leavitt's Diamond, explain why the implementation may fail and name two non-technology adjustments that should be considered.
options: Technology upgrades alone are sufficient if the database migration is correct.

Leavitt's Diamond means balancing people, processes, technology, and structure; changing only the technology can fail because users, workflows, roles, and reporting lines may not fit the new system. The company should train users and IT staff, redesign sales/support processes, and clarify ownership or reporting responsibilities around CRM data.
The main risk is that CRM systems are always strategic systems, so operational users should not use them.
The company should avoid organizational change because structure is independent from information systems.
questions.expected: Leavitt's Diamond means balancing people, processes, technology, and structure; changing only the technology can fail because users, workflows, roles, and reporting lines may not fit the new system. The company should train users and IT staff, redesign sales/support processes, and clarify ownership or reporting responsibilities around CRM data.

questions.question: Name two IT infrastructure component categories and, for each, describe its role and how it connects to at least one other component category. Your answer should be suitable for an $8$-point past-exam style question.
options: Applications run only on client devices; networking is unrelated to databases.

Databases store and retrieve organizational data for applications; they connect to applications and servers because applications query database services hosted on server infrastructure. Networking provides communication between clients, servers, storage, and external services; it connects client devices to application or database servers and can support backups or replication to remote storage.
Security is a separate component that only protects the data center building; storage is temporary memory used by CPUs.
Servers only provide physical space; applications are not infrastructure components.
questions.expected: Databases store and retrieve organizational data for applications; they connect to applications and servers because applications query database services hosted on server infrastructure. Networking provides communication between clients, servers, storage, and external services; it connects client devices to application or database servers and can support backups or replication to remote storage.

questions.question: Distinguish an information system from IT infrastructure. Give one example of each and explain their relationship.
options: An information system is the integrated set of components that collect, store, process, and deliver information for decisions and operations; an example is an ERP system used for finance and inventory. IT infrastructure is the underlying foundation of servers, storage, networks, operating systems, databases, security, and facilities; an example is a cloud-hosted server and database platform. The information system depends on the infrastructure to run and deliver value.
IT infrastructure is the business process, while an information system is only the physical server room.
Information systems and IT infrastructure are synonyms, so no distinction is needed.
An information system is always personal, while IT infrastructure is always interorganizational.
questions.expected: An information system is the integrated set of components that collect, store, process, and deliver information for decisions and operations; an example is an ERP system used for finance and inventory. IT infrastructure is the underlying foundation of servers, storage, networks, operating systems, databases, security, and facilities; an example is a cloud-hosted server and database platform. The information system depends on the infrastructure to run and deliver value.

questions.question: A firm wants to move from on-premise infrastructure to a higher-level cloud service model. Explain two benefits and two risks of moving upward from IaaS toward PaaS or SaaS.
options: Moving upward can reduce upfront capital expense, speed deployment, improve scalability, and shift updates or patching to the provider. The tradeoffs are less control over lower layers, reduced customization, vendor lock-in, and dependency on the provider's availability and security posture.
Moving upward always increases customization and removes vendor dependency.
The only benefit is that the customer manages more operating-system patches.
The only risk is that client devices disappear from the infrastructure stack.
questions.expected: Moving upward can reduce upfront capital expense, speed deployment, improve scalability, and shift updates or patching to the provider. The tradeoffs are less control over lower layers, reduced customization, vendor lock-in, and dependency on the provider's availability and security posture.

questions.question: A company has $480$ software users. $35\%$ use an unauthorized file-sharing app, and $25\%$ of those shadow-IT users also store customer data in it. How many users both use the unauthorized app and store customer data there?
options: $42$ users. Method: unauthorized users $= 480 \times 0.35 = 168$; risky users $= 168 \times 0.25 = 42$.
$168$ users, because that is the shadow-IT group.
$120$ users, because $25\%$ of all users store customer data there.
questions.expected: $42$ users. Method: unauthorized users $= 480 \times 0.35 = 168$; risky users $= 168 \times 0.25 = 42$.

questions.question: An on-premise deployment requires the customer to manage $10$ infrastructure component categories. In IaaS the provider manages $5$ categories, in PaaS the provider manages $7$ categories, and in SaaS the provider manages $9$ categories. What percentage of component categories does the customer still manage in each model?
options: On-premise: $100\%$; IaaS: $50\%$; PaaS: $30\%$; SaaS: $10\%$. Method: customer-managed categories $= 10 -$ provider-managed categories, then divide by $10$ and multiply by $100\%$.
questions.expected: On-premise: $100\%$; IaaS: $50\%$; PaaS: $30\%$; SaaS: $10\%$. Method: customer-managed categories $= 10 -$ provider-managed categories, then divide by $10$ and multiply by $100\%$.

questions.question: A BYOD program has $320$ employees. Each employee connects $1.5$ personal devices on average. Security estimates that $18\%$ of personal devices are missing required patches. How many unpatched BYOD devices should IT expect?
options: $86.4$, so about $86$ or $87$ devices depending on rounding policy. Method: total devices $= 320 \times 1.5 = 480$; unpatched devices $= 480 \times 0.18 = 86.4$.
$57.6$, because $18\%$ should be applied only to employees.
$480$, because every BYOD device is unpatched.
questions.expected: $86.4$, so about $86$ or $87$ devices depending on rounding policy. Method: total devices $= 320 \times 1.5 = 480$; unpatched devices $= 480 \times 0.18 = 86.4$.

questions.question: A transaction-processing system handles $12{,}000$ orders per day. A planned expansion increases volume by $40\%$, and a cloud provider can add capacity in blocks of $2{,}000$ orders per day. How many additional capacity blocks are needed to handle the new expected volume above the current capacity?
options: $3$ blocks. Method: added demand $= 12{,}000 \times 0.40 = 4{,}800$ orders per day; blocks needed $= \lceil 4{,}800 / 2{,}000 \rceil = \lceil 2.4 \rceil = 3$.
$6$ blocks, because the final workload is $16{,}800$ and $16{,}800 / 2{,}000 = 8.4$.
questions.expected: $3$ blocks. Method: added demand $= 12{,}000 \times 0.40 = 4{,}800$ orders per day; blocks needed $= \lceil 4{,}800 / 2{,}000 \rceil = \lceil 2.4 \rceil = 3$.

questions.question: Which option best classifies a shared project-management system used only by a product team of $12$ people inside one company?
questions.expected: Workgroup information system

questions.question: A company uses a cloud database service where the provider manages data centers, networking, storage, servers, virtualization, operating systems, and the database platform. The customer manages the application code and application-level security configuration. Which service model is this closest to?
questions.expected: PaaS

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders the infrastructure evolution eras from earliest to latest?
options: Cloud/mobile, web/internet, client-server, personal computer, mainframe
Mainframe, personal computer, client-server, web/internet, cloud/mobile
Personal computer, mainframe, client-server, cloud/mobile, web/internet
Mainframe, client-server, personal computer, cloud/mobile, web/internet
questions.expected: Mainframe, personal computer, client-server, web/internet, cloud/mobile

questions.question: Which statement best matches the role of security as an IT infrastructure component?
options: Security is only a physical data-center function and does not affect applications or networks.
Security is a layer that includes access controls, encryption, authentication, and monitoring across applications, operating systems, networks, and facilities.
Security replaces databases because encrypted data no longer needs storage.
Security is managed only by end users in every service model.
questions.expected: Security is a layer that includes access controls, encryption, authentication, and monitoring across applications, operating systems, networks, and facilities.

questions.question: True or false: In SaaS, the customer normally manages operating systems, virtualization, servers, storage, networking, and data centers.
options: True. SaaS shifts only applications to the provider, while the customer keeps the infrastructure stack.

False. In SaaS the provider manages almost the whole stack; the customer mainly configures and uses the application rather than managing OS, virtualization, servers, storage, networking, or data centers.
True. SaaS and on-premise have the same management split.
False. SaaS eliminates the need for application configuration entirely.
questions.expected: False. In SaaS the provider manages almost the whole stack; the customer mainly configures and uses the application rather than managing OS, virtualization, servers, storage, networking, or data centers.

questions.question: True or false: Shadow IT is harmless when the software improves productivity, because it remains outside formal IT infrastructure.
options: True. Productivity gains mean security and compliance concerns are no longer relevant.
False. Shadow IT can improve productivity, but unauthorized systems still create security, data governance, integration, and compliance risks because IT lacks oversight.
True. Systems outside IT oversight cannot connect to organizational data.
False. Shadow IT is only a problem when it is hosted on-premise.
questions.expected: False. Shadow IT can improve productivity, but unauthorized systems still create security, data governance, integration, and compliance risks because IT lacks oversight.

questions.question: Write pseudocode for a classifier that takes a system description with fields `user_count`, `same_team`, `whole_organization`, and `external_partners`, and returns the correct sphere of influence: personal, workgroup, enterprise, or interorganizational. Prioritize external partners over internal scope when both are present.

Write pseudocode for a function `customerManagedLayers(model)` that returns the IT infrastructure layers managed by the customer for `On-Premise`, `IaaS`, `PaaS`, and `SaaS`, using the chapter's service-model split.

A hospital introduces a new electronic medication administration system but only installs the software. Nurses receive no workflow training, pharmacy approval steps remain unchanged, and ward responsibilities are not updated. Which Leavitt's Diamond diagnosis best explains why adoption is likely to fail?
options: The technology corner changed, but people, processes, and structure were not adjusted to match it.
The people corner changed, but technology, processes, and structure were left unchanged.
The process corner changed, but technology, people, and structure were left unchanged.
The structure corner changed, but technology, people, and processes were left unchanged.
The system failed because Leavitt's Diamond applies only to hardware infrastructure, not information systems.
questions.expected: The technology corner changed, but people, processes, and structure were not adjusted to match it.

questions.question: Which option best classifies a supplier portal where a manufacturer and its external component suppliers exchange forecasts, purchase orders, and shipment confirmations?
questions.expected: Interorganizational information system

questions.question: A retail chain uses one system to record every sale at checkout, another to summarize weekly regional sales for store managers, and a third to help executives decide whether to enter a new country. Which mapping is most accurate?
options: Checkout is operational, weekly regional summaries are tactical, and country-entry analysis is strategic.
Checkout is tactical, weekly regional summaries are operational, and country-entry analysis is strategic.
Checkout is strategic, weekly regional summaries are tactical, and country-entry analysis is operational.
Checkout is operational, weekly regional summaries are strategic, and country-entry analysis is tactical.
All three are operational because they use company data.
questions.expected: Checkout is operational, weekly regional summaries are tactical, and country-entry analysis is strategic.

questions.question: Which statement best describes how databases and storage differ as infrastructure components?
options: Databases organize, query, and retrieve data for applications, while storage provides the persistent physical or logical capacity where data is kept.
Databases are end-user devices, while storage is the authentication layer protecting those devices.
Databases provide network connectivity, while storage executes business logic for users.
Databases replace applications in SaaS, while storage exists only in on-premise deployments.
Databases are physical facilities, while storage is the operating system installed in those facilities.
questions.expected: Databases organize, query, and retrieve data for applications, while storage provides the persistent physical or logical capacity where data is kept.

questions.question: A company wants the provider to manage databases, operating systems, virtualization, servers, storage, networking, and data centers, while the company keeps responsibility for application logic and security configuration. Which service model fits best?
questions.expected: PaaS

questions.question: Which infrastructure evolution era is most directly associated with centralized computing power accessed through dumb terminals?
questions.expected: Mainframe era

questions.question: True or false: Moving from IaaS to PaaS usually reduces the customer's operational responsibility, but it can also reduce direct control over database and operating-system configuration.
options: It depends only on user count.
Only when no security layer exists.
questions.expected: True. In PaaS, the provider adds management of databases and operating systems compared with IaaS. That shift can speed deployment and patching, but it also limits low-level customization.

questions.question: True or false: A CRM used by every sales, marketing, and service employee in one company is a workgroup information system because it supports collaboration.
options: Only if it has fewer than $10$ users.
Only if external suppliers also use it.
questions.expected: False. Because it supports a whole organization or major organization-wide function, it is better classified as an enterprise information system, not merely a workgroup system.

questions.question: True or false: Security is best treated as a single standalone layer that connects only to applications, because network encryption, operating-system access control, and data-center monitoring are outside the security component.
questions.expected: False. Security permeates multiple infrastructure layers, including applications, networks, operating systems, databases, and physical facilities.

questions.question: True or false: Scalability is only a concern after a system fails, because infrastructure planning should be based exclusively on current transaction volume.
options: Only when there are $0$ mobile users.
questions.expected: False. Scalability is the ability to expand capacity as demand grows, so it must be considered before growth causes performance or availability problems.

questions.question: True or false: BYOD can create infrastructure-management risk even when employees use approved applications, because personal devices may vary in patch level, configuration, and exposure to loss or malware.
options: Only if the system is interorganizational.
Only if the provider manages no layers.
Only if the application is not browser-based.
questions.expected: True. BYOD increases the attack surface and complicates patch management because organizational data and systems are accessed from devices the organization may not fully control.

questions.question: A SaaS vendor promises $99.9\\%$ monthly availability for a system used continuously over a $30$-day month. Calculate the maximum downtime allowed in minutes and explain why availability matters as an infrastructure-management concern.
questions.expected: A $30$-day month has $30 \times 24 \times 60 = 43{,}200$ minutes. Allowed unavailability is $100\% - 99.9\% = 0.1\% = 0.001$, so maximum downtime is $43{,}200 \times 0.001 = 43.2$ minutes. Availability matters because users and business processes depend on the system being reachable; outages can stop operations even when the provider manages most infrastructure layers.

questions.question: Name two IT infrastructure component categories not including security. For each, describe its role and one connection to another component category.
questions.expected: A strong answer names two valid categories such as servers and networking. Servers provide computing resources that run applications, databases, or middleware; they connect to storage for persistent data and to client devices through networking. Networking provides communication across LANs, WANs, or the internet; it links client devices, servers, storage systems, and external services so information can move between infrastructure layers.

questions.question: A firm currently manages $10$ infrastructure layers on-premise. It moves first to IaaS, where the provider manages $5$ layers, and later to PaaS, where the provider manages $7$ layers. Calculate the percentage-point increase in provider-managed responsibility from IaaS to PaaS, and identify the extra layers shifted to the provider.
questions.expected: In IaaS the provider manages $5$ out of $10$ layers, or $50\%$. In PaaS the provider manages $7$ out of $10$ layers, or $70\%$. The increase is $70\% - 50\% = 20$ percentage points. The additional layers shifted from customer to provider are databases and operating systems.

questions.question: Classify each system by sphere of influence and justify briefly: a student's private revision spreadsheet, a shared Kanban board for a $6$-person audit team, an ERP used across a university, and an EDI link between the university and an external payroll provider.
questions.expected: The private revision spreadsheet is a personal information system because it supports one user. The $6$-person Kanban board is a workgroup information system because it supports a team. The ERP is an enterprise information system because it supports organization-wide processes. The EDI link is an interorganizational information system because it spans two organizations.
